description: Closed vocabulary of valid `canonical_type` values for entities admitted to the entities table. This file is the single source of truth that the LDU consults at write time (admit_candidate / subtype_validator) and the GDU enforces via the trg_enforce_entities_governance trigger AND the entities_canonical_type_check storage constraint (generated from valid_entity_subtypes()). Each subtype declares its canonical name plus aliases (common LLM drift and synonyms) and ner_tags (Stanford/spaCy raw output) that should be normalized to it. Types not in this file (and not in cross_category_routes) get rejected from the entities table at LDU write time. As of v0.6.0, places are first-class entity subtypes (migration 118 unified the places table into entities + the place_attributes spatial sidecar); they are NO LONGER routed out via cross_category_routes.
rationale: Without a closed entity-subtype vocabulary, the LDU accepts whatever the LLM produces — 449 distinct subtype strings ended up in entities, of which only 13 were valid per the GDU pack. Cleaning after admission (cross_category_migrator) is detection, not prevention. The architecture pitch (LDU open mouth → GDU locked jaw) requires a write-time check. v0.6.0 closes the places fracture: migration 118 made places entities, but the pack + constraint still routed them out, so event_validator crash-looped trying to UPDATE place-typed rows the constraint rejected. Places are now accepted subtypes and the storage constraint is generated from this file so the two can never drift again.

person.description: An individual human being. Includes historical figures, fictional persons named as individuals, and entities self-identifying as individuals.

organization.description: A formal collective entity (company, NGO, club, military branch, etc.). NOT used for government agencies (use government_agency).

government_agency.description: A governmental body at any level — federal, state, municipal, supranational, intergovernmental.

facility.description: A physical built structure or compound with a fixed location. NOT a geographic area (use a place subtype: named_area, country, city, etc.).

mass_media.description: An entity whose primary function is mass communication of information.

aircraft.description: An air or space vehicle. Specific named aircraft (tail numbers, named craft); for vehicle types use product.

vessel.description: A water-going vehicle. Specific named vessels (MMSI/IMO); for vessel types use product.

vehicle.description: A land-going vehicle. Specific named/registered vehicles (VIN/plate); for vehicle types use product.

device.description: A discrete physical device that is not a vehicle or weapon (sensors, IoT, instruments, etc.).

weapon_system.description: A weapons platform or system. Specific named/serialized systems; for weapon types use product.

account.description: A digital account / identity on a platform (social media handle, email account, etc.).

unit.description: A military or paramilitary unit at any echelon.

product.description: A commercially-produced item, service, or branded model. Used for product *types* (e.g., 'F-35'); for specific tail-numbered units use aircraft.

country.description: A sovereign state. Spatial data (ISO codes, geometry, hierarchy) lives in the place_attributes sidecar keyed on entity_id.

city.description: A populated settlement. Spatial data lives in place_attributes.

admin_region.description: A sub-national administrative division (US state, province, oblast, county, etc.). For sovereign states use country.

named_area.description: A named geographic area without a fixed administrative boundary (continent, island, mountain, river, region-by-name, point-of-interest, airspace). Default place subtype for ambiguous GPE/LOC tags.

maritime_area.description: A body of water or maritime feature (sea, strait, gulf, ocean, lake).

facility_location.description: A geographic place defined by an infrastructure function (airport, seaport, station, border crossing). For the built structure itself use facility.

cross_category_routes.description: Subtype strings that are genuinely non-entity — route to the named (category, subtype) instead of admitting to entities. Places are NO LONGER routed here: as of v0.6.0 they are first-class entity subtypes (see migration 118). Remaining routes are temporal (chronicle), abstract (topic), source (document), and quantitative (form) referents that belong in their own substrates.

drop_types.description: Subtype strings that are pure LLM/NER drift — meaningless fragments. Reject at LDU write time, do not route anywhere.
